 13 weather alerts in effect Will more storms hit Arizona? Here’s the weekend timeline 
 Friday is a First Alert Weather Day, with a high chance of rain and a chance of thunderstorms as well. Pete Mangione has the latest on our Halloween forecast. By Holly Bock Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 6:07 AM MST | Updated : 6 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — A flood warning is in effect Friday until 10:45 p.m. in the northeast Valley, with showers and thunderstorms across the area. This activity will die down overnight and we will get a bit of a break by Saturday morning. 
 Flash Flood Warning including Maricopa County, AZ until 10:45 PM MST pic.twitter.com/mBiFr5zWil 
— NWS Phoenix (@NWSPhoenix) October 31, 2026 
 The first half of Saturday looks pretty quiet, but by the evening, our rain chances will pick up as the second weather system moves through Saturday evening into Sunday. 
 On Sunday, we can expect a long-duration rain event of light to moderate rainfall. Expect highs around 78 degrees Saturday, and a high temperature of 70 degrees on Sunday. 
 A flood watch will be issued once again for Saturday night through Monday morning for most of Arizona, minus western Arizona. S
 Shower activity will be more scattered through Saturday evening and overnight and become more widespread across Arizona by Sunday morning. 
 Download the First Alert Weather App    First Alert Weather Radar    Rainfall Totals While we aren’t necessarily thinking these will be strong storms that dump a lot of rain at once, flooding is possible mainly because this looks to be a long-duration event with on-and-off rain expected for several hours Sunday. 
 Drier air will move into the region by Sunday evening, and while we may still see some lingering showers across eastern Arizona Monday morning, it should be a quiet start to the workweek in Phoenix.
